BVD features for EMI · corrosion mass-loss · 9 Oct 2026

Raw impedance vs BVD features: what was wrong, what we fixed, what we can claim

A CNN trained on four BVD parameters is compared with the same CNN trained on the full impedance spectrum, on three steel probes, with leave-one-probe-out validation.

3.7 gBVD features, held-out RMSE (R² 0.93)
15.4 graw impedance, held-out RMSE (R² −0.30). Guessing the training mean gives 14.7 g
3 / 3held-out probes where BVD beats raw
0.7 g vs 8.4 gtrain-to-held-out gap: BVD vs raw

1 · The claim we want to support

A BVD fit turns one measurement into a few physically meaningful numbers. Raw impedance gives the network 3000 frequency points per measurement and about 28 real training rows to learn from. The claim: BVD features generalize to an unseen probe better than raw impedance does.

2 · What was wrong with the original evaluation

The original notebook reported R² 0.97 and about 2.5 g. Reading the training and scoring code showed the number was not a measure of generalization.

validation = test

The held-out probe steered training

Early stopping, the learning-rate schedule and the kept weights all read the loss of the probe that was then reported.

synthetic points scored

About 95% of the scored rows were synthetic

20 interpolated points were inserted between each pair of real rows, including for the held-out probe, and they were scored.

augmentation before split

Interpolation and noise used all probes

The noise scale came from all three probes, and the held-out probe was interpolated like the others.

bug

"Real RMSE" was the overall train RMSE

The augmentation flags were built on the pooled rows, so they never matched the sequences and the mask was always all-True.

input quality

Cubic splines overshoot

Interpolated inputs such as rel_R1 reached −0.7 where the real values were about −0.05. The model trained and scored on values that never occur.

model

Norm layers and a huge learning rate

Group/batch norm removes absolute feature level when the window is 1, and Adam at lr 0.1 made the validation curve spiky, so early stopping picked a lucky dip.

What the selection hid

Held-out MSE (g²) at the epoch the original loop would have kept, vs at the end of training (original loop re-run with a smaller learning rate).

Is raw just badly set up?

More checks against "unfair raw"

  • Best epoch picked on the held-out probe: raw 12.1 g, BVD 4.1 g.
  • Similar size: 3,409 parameters (raw) vs 3,473 (BVD).
  • Inputs: 200 for raw (100 bins × 2 channels), 4 for BVD, about 28 real training rows either way.
Predictions over time for each held-out probe

6 · Why there is no separate test set

The probe is the only valid unit to split on

Readings from one probe are near-duplicates, so a row-level split would put almost identical data in train and test and measure memorization.

Only three probes

A separate test probe leaves two for everything else. Tuning inside those two means each model sees one probe, too little to select anything. One test probe would also give a single noisy score instead of three.

Leave-one-probe-out is the standard answer

Each probe is scored by a model that never saw it, and nothing in training reads it. The three scores use all the data.

The claim is a comparison

Both arms run under the same protocol, so "BVD generalizes better than raw" does not need an unbiased absolute RMSE.

7 · Criticism and our answers

CriticismAnswerStatus
The held-out probe was also the validation setNo stopping, checkpoint or schedule reads it any more. The settings were still chosen by looking at these folds, so the absolute errors are best-case.loop fixed, selection disclosed
Synthetic points were scoredReal held-out rows only (15, 13 and 15 rows).fixed
Augmentation before the splitDone inside each fold, on the training probes only, together with the scaler and the noise scale.fixed
"Why no test set?"Section 6. The next step is an independent probe.limitation
BVD got more tuning than rawTrue. Raw got 13 setups, plus an oracle-epoch check. None approaches BVD, so the ranking holds, but the size of the gap is probably inflated.limitation
The team's fair rerun scored 9.6 g, not 3.7 gThat rerun chose the epoch count on inner folds of the training probes. Our 3.7 g also used settings picked on these folds. The honest figure for this model probably lies between the two.best-case
BVD depends on rel_L1By design. L1 is the acoustic-mass parameter. It is fixed at 0.020 H on each probe's first fit because all probes start with the same weight, and it can only decrease afterwards because the probe only loses mass. The values are tiny (about 1e-6) because only the relative change is used. rel_C1 is left out because L1 and C1 overlap in information (fr depends on L1·C1). Without rel_L1 the other parameters do not predict mass loss across probes (25 to 34 g). A likely question is whether a monotone L1 behaves like a time proxy; we state openly that the result rests on this channel.design choice
Mass loss is close to linear in elapsed timeYes (about 1.1 g/day on all three probes), and a straight line in time scores about 2.3 to 2.5 g. We do not claim BVD beats a time model. The claim is BVD versus raw impedance, as the same time structure is available to both arms.context

How L1 is handled in the fit (design choice)

L1_BASELINE = 0.020  # H                               # bvd_utils.fit_bvd: same starting weight for every probe
if first_fit:  bounds[3] = (L1_BASELINE, L1_BASELINE)   # first fit: L1 fixed at the baseline
high = min(high, prev_L1 * (1 + max_L1_increase))        # later fits: L1 may not increase (the probe only loses mass)
# l1_change_penalty = 50 keeps L1 close to the previous fit

Only the relative change of L1 enters the model, so the small absolute change is not a problem. rel_C1 is dropped for now because L1 and C1 carry overlapping information.

8 · What we can and cannot claim

we can say
  • Under leave-one-probe-out on three probes, BVD features beat raw impedance on all three held-out probes (3.7 g vs 15.4 g).
  • No raw setup came meaningfully below predicting the training mean (the best was 1.3 g lower, 13 setups tried).
  • The BVD model has a small train-to-held-out gap (0.7 g); the raw model a large one (8.4 g).
  • The fitted L1 (the mass channel, fixed baseline, relative change only) is what carries this result.
we cannot say
  • That 3.7 g is the error on a new probe: settings were chosen on these folds and there is no independent test.
  • That parameters other than L1 carry the mass-loss signal in this dataset: without rel_L1 the model fails.
  • That the gap size is exact: BVD was tuned more than raw.

Suggested wording. With leave-one-probe-out validation on three probes, a CNN trained on four BVD-derived features reached 3.7 g held-out RMSE (R² 0.93) and beat a CNN trained on the full impedance spectrum on all three probes (15.4 g, no better than the training mean), with a small train-to-held-out gap (0.7 g vs 8.4 g). Settings were chosen on the same folds, so the absolute errors are best-case estimates, and confirming generalization requires an independent probe.

9 · Next steps

1 · Different starting weights

The fixed L1 baseline assumes every probe starts with the same weight. Test a probe with a different starting weight, or set the baseline from the measured weight.

2 · Equal tuning budget

Give BVD and raw the same search space and number of runs, chosen inside the training probes only.

3 · An independent probe

One new probe, never looked at, scored once. That replaces the missing test set.
